name: Bavdegalutamide (ARV-110)
reasoning: Target: androgen receptor (AR). Modality: PROTAC degrader.
Querying ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed for pivotal trials, endpoints, and attrition signals…
Cross-checking openFDA + FDA approval records for the exact regulatory pathway…
Connecting research → clinical → regulatory; every claim 3-vote cross-checked, unsourced items flagged.

claims.text: Bavdegalutamide (ARV-110) is a heterobifunctional PROTAC that degrades the androgen receptor by recruiting the cereblon E3 ubiquitin ligase, driving AR polyubiquitination and proteasomal destruction — the defining modality of the asset (event-driven degradation, not occupancy-based inhibition).
claims.quote: Bavdegalutamide (ARV-110) is a PROTAC protein degrader designed to target AR for ubiquitination and degradation through recruitment of the E3 ubiquitin ligase substrate adapter cereblon

claims.text: The molecular-target rationale: AR signaling is the principal driver of prostate cancer, and AR alterations (mutation, amplification, splicing) drive resistance to standard AR-pathway inhibitors — the exact escape mechanisms a degrader is built to overcome by removing the protein rather than blocking its ligand pocket.
claims.quote: Androgen receptor (AR) signaling is the principal driver of prostate cancer

claims.text: Potency benchmark supporting the degrader thesis: ARV-110 drove near-complete AR loss in prostate cancer cell lines at low-nanomolar concentrations, consistent with catalytic degradation.
claims.quote: Bavdegalutamide induced robust degradation of AR at a DC50 of 1 nmol/L in LNCaP and VCaP cells, with >95% of AR degraded in both prostate cancer cell lines

claims.text: The preclinical result that predicted the clinical biomarker: ARV-110 degraded the T878A and H875Y mutant ARs as effectively as wild-type — the same mutations that later marked the responder subgroup in the clinic, tying mechanism directly to patient selection.
claims.quote: Four of the six AR-mutant proteins tested (F877L, T878A, M896V, and H875Y) were degraded with similar potency to WT AR

claims.text: Attrition / limitation signal (mechanistic ceiling): ARV-110 did not degrade the AR-V7 splice variant, which lacks the ligand-binding domain the PROTAC engages, and cleared L702H-mutant AR only at reduced potency. This pre-defines a non-responder population and is exactly why ARDENT carved out an AR L702H / AR-V7 subgroup as expected non-responders.
claims.quote: did not induce the degradation of AR splice variant 7, which lacks the AR LBD

claims.text: The pivotal early-phase trial: ARDENT (NCT03888612), a first-in-human Phase 1/2 open-label dose-escalation and cohort-expansion study of ARV-110 in mCRPC, sponsored by Arvinas Inc., enrolled 248 patients with PSA response rate (PCWG3) and RECIST response rate as the primary anti-tumor endpoints; the study is now listed as Completed.
claims.quote: A Phase 1/2, Open-label, Dose Escalation, and Cohort Expansion Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of ARV-110 in Patients With Metastatic Castration Resistant Prostate Cancer

claims.text: Key efficacy signal, concentrated in the biomarker-defined subgroup: roughly half of patients whose tumors carried AR T878X/H875Y mutations had significant PSA declines on ARV-110 in the Phase 2 ARDENT cohort (reported at ASCO GU 2022) — matching the mutant ARs the degrader was shown preclinically to clear.
claims.quote: Approximately 50% of patients with these mutations treated with ARV-110 experienced a significant reduction in prostate-specific antigen levels

claims.text: Dose and timing of the Phase 2 expansion: the ARDENT Phase 2 cohort opened in October 2020 at the 420 mg once-daily dose, the dose at which the biomarker-subgroup activity was reported.
claims.quote: its phase II clinical study (ARDENT) commenced in October 2020 at a dose of 420 mg

claims.text: The EXACT and only FDA program obtained: Fast Track designation, granted by the U.S. FDA and announced May 29, 2019. Fast Track is an expedited-development/review program — distinct from Breakthrough Therapy, Accelerated Approval, Priority Review, RTOR, and Project Orbis. ARV-110 never received FDA approval; this designation is not an approval or an efficacy endorsement.
claims.quote: ARV-110, has been granted Fast Track designation by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)

claims.text: Exact indication wording covered by the Fast Track designation: late-line mCRPC after two or more prior systemic therapies — a heavily pretreated, post-ARPI population, consistent with the ARDENT enrollment criteria.
claims.quote: treatment of men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) whose disease has progressed after treatment with two or more systemic therapies
